content.text: The agreement contains no MFN or most-favoured-customer mechanic in either direction, which matches the preferred position for this rule.

input.quote: (a) During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work. Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
input.rationale: This rule is directional: it is triggered only where the Customer must extend to the Vendor terms no less favourable than those given to third parties, or must match third-party offers. The compensation provisions in § 3 set pricing solely by reference to each Statement of Work on a time-and-materials basis (with a Contractor-side right to change rates on 30 days' notice, addressed under the pricing/uplift rules rather than here). Searches across the full agreement for "most favoured", "most favored", "favorable", "no less" and third-party comparison language return no most-favoured-nation, most-favoured-customer, benchmarking or rate-matching mechanic anywhere in the document, and the only sections present (§§ 1, 3–7) contain no such construct. There is therefore no MFN obligation burdening Clear Capital, which is the playbook's preferred position — the absence of the clause is the outcome we want, so this is compliant rather than "missing" and no redline is warranted. Noted for completeness only: the agreement likewise grants us no MFN pricing in our favour, which would be welcome but is an upside ask, not a deviation under this rule.
